title: Analyzing Cachectic Phenotypes in Drosophila Larvae Muscle and Fat Body
author: Dark, Cheung, et al.
materials: HCS LipidTOX™ Deep Red Neutral Lipid Stain
Timing: Either 1.5h, or overnight, as required

steps.title: Stain muscle fillets with phalloidin
steps.instruction: Remove the existing PBST from each fixed larval muscle fillet and add phalloidin diluted in 0.3% PBST, using enough solution to fully cover the fillet (≈200 µL per well in a 6‑place porcelain spotting plate). Use any fluorescently‑labeled phalloidin at a 1:200 dilution (as recommended by the manufacturer). Stain in the dark for either 1 hour at room temperature (RT) or up to 24 hours at 4 °C. After staining, discard the phalloidin solution and wash the fillets three times with 0.3% PBST (10 min each wash at RT). Finally, replace the wash buffer with 50 % glycerol to fully cover the fillets. Fillets can be stored at 4 °C in 50 % glycerol for up to one week; keep the spotting plate in a moist chamber (e.g., a moist paper towel in a dark box) to prevent drying.

substeps.instruction: Remove PBST from each fillet.
Add phalloidin diluted in 0.3% PBST (200 µL per well).
Incubate in the dark: 1 h at RT or ≤24 h at 4 °C.
Wash 3× with 0.3% PBST, 10 min each at RT.
Add 50 % glycerol to cover fillets.
Store at 4 °C (up to 1 week) in a moist chamber if needed.

steps.title: Image analysis of muscle fillet detachment
steps.instruction: Organize stitched images into separate folders for each experimental condition, creating an ‘Input’ and an ‘Output’ subfolder within each. Import the “oir to tiff” macro into FIJI and run it, selecting the appropriate Input and Output folders to convert images to TIFF format. Then import the “Fillet muscle detachment analysis” macro and run it, selecting the folder containing the converted TIFFs as Input. For each fillet, draw a square ROI (hold Shift for a perfect square), then draw an ROI around the fillet itself, confirm the suggested threshold and ROI when prompted, and click OK. The macro will generate a .csv file reporting the percentage of area occupied by fluorescent pixels within the fillet ROI. Repeat the process for all fillets in the folder and for each experimental group.

substeps.instruction: Create ‘Input’ and ‘Output’ folders for each condition.
Drag‑and‑drop the “oir to tiff” macro into FIJI and run it.
Select the condition’s Input folder and an Output folder; run conversion.
Drag‑and‑drop the “Fillet muscle detachment analysis” macro into FIJI and run it.
Select the folder with converted TIFFs as Input.
For each fillet:
a. Draw a square ROI around the fillet (Shift‑click for perfect square).
b. Draw an ROI tightly around the fillet boundary.
c. Confirm the auto‑threshold and ROI when prompted, then click OK.
d. Allow the macro to output a .csv file with the muscle area percentage.
Proceed through all fillets; repeat steps 2‑9 for each experimental group.

steps.title: Stain fat body with DAPI/phalloidin or LipidTOX
steps.instruction: For each fixed larval fat body, choose either DAPI/phalloidin staining or LipidTOX staining. For DAPI/phalloidin, remove 0.2 % PBST and add a mixture of DAPI (1:100) and phalloidin (1:200) diluted in 200 µL of 0.2 % PBST per well of the spotting plate. For LipidTOX, remove PBS and add LipidTOX diluted 1:1,000 in 200 µL of PBS per well. Incubate the fillets in the dark for 1 hour at RT without agitation. After staining, replace the staining solution with 200 µL of the corresponding wash buffer (0.2 % PBST for DAPI/phalloidin, PBS for LipidTOX) and wash three times, 10 min each at RT.

substeps.instruction: Choose staining method:
a. DAPI/phalloidin: remove 0.2 % PBST, add DAPI (1:100) + phalloidin (1:200) in 200 µL 0.2 % PBST.
b. LipidTOX: remove PBS, add LipidTOX (1:1,000) in 200 µL PBS.
Incubate in the dark for 1 hour at RT without agitation.
Wash:
a. For DAPI/phalloidin, replace with 200 µL 0.2 % PBST and wash 3×, 10 min each at RT.
b. For LipidTOX, replace with 200 µL PBS and wash 3×, 10 min each at RT.

steps.title: Statistical analysis of quantified data
steps.instruction: Analyze the quantitative outputs (e.g., muscle area percentages or lipid droplet metrics) using appropriate statistical tests such as Student’s t‑test, one‑way ANOVA, or their non‑parametric equivalents, depending on experimental design. Plot all data using GraphPad Prism version 9.0.2 for Windows.

description: Drosophila larvae have been increasingly used to study the wasting phenotypes seen in cachexia (Ding et al., 2021; Figueroa-Clarevega and Bilder, 2015; Kwon et al., 2015; Newton et al., 2020; Santabárbara-Ruiz and Léopold, 2021; Song et al., 2019). In our recent study, we have shown that tumor bearing animals exhibit several wasting phenotypes including muscle detachment, as well as fat body lipid droplet accumulation and extracellular matrix (ECM) mislocalization (Lodge et al., 2021). As utilization of Drosophila larvae to study cachexia has become increasingly popular, and the field is rapidly expanding, it is important to have standardized and quantitative methods that enable phenotypes between studies or in different genetic models to be easily compared. Here we present a collection of protocols for systematic quantification of cachexia phenotypes in the Drosophila muscle and the fat body, using semi-automated FIJI macros (Schindelin et al., 2012). While these protocols are devised to primarily characterize tumor induced cachexia phenotypes, they can also be used in other disease settings such as muscular dystrophy (muscle detachment) or obesity (lipid droplet accumulation). Furthermore, these quantitative methods can also be adapted for drug or genetic screens, to ensure easy and rapid comparison between experimental settings.
